1 # Skills 2 3 English | [中文](skills.zh.md) 4 5 The [skill capability family](../../packages/skill) includes the Service Definition ([dsh-skill](../../packages/skill/skill), `ctx.skills`), the local Service Provider ([dsh-skill-filesystem](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem)), the optional packaged badge provider ([dsh-skill-badge](../../packages/skill/skill-badge)), and the Consumer ([dsh-tool-skill](../../packages/skill/tool-skill)). The registry merges provider catalogs across its host and per-scope layers; providers contribute local or packaged skills; the Consumer owns the initial and replacement catalogs plus the model-facing `skill` tool. Skills are optional instructions, not session events, so their vocabulary lives here rather than in [core.md](core.md). 6 7 Source: [`packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts), [`packages/skill/skill-filesystem/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/skill-filesystem/src/index.ts), [`packages/skill/skill-badge/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/skill-badge/src/index.ts), and [`packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts`](../../packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts). 8 9 ## Provider registry 10 11 `ctx.skills` combines local, embedded, remote, or other providers. Registration is synchronous; remote initialization and discovery belong in awaited `list()`. Provider objects, options, and candidates are borrowed readonly, while semantic fields are validated. 12 13 The registry is host+per-scope layered, the shape the [tools registry](tools.md) established over [dsh-scope](../../packages/core/scope): a registration files into the layer of its calling context's scope, so host rows and repository plugins land in the global layer while a plugin mounted by an agent preset's standing composition lands in that preset's layer, and provider names are unique per layer rather than process-wide. A read merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain — the nearest layer's entry wins a duplicate skill name outright, and the rank order below decides duplicates only within one layer. Discovery caches are keyed by the resolved scope chain, so re-parenting a scope (a blank-session recompose) is visible to the next read without a registry mutation. 14 15 Within one layer, duplicate names resolve by rank, provider order, then local order; summaries sort by name. A rejected `list()` is logged and omitted from an incomplete observation, while an explicit incomplete observation contributes usable candidates without making the result cacheable; malformed candidates fail fast. Each provider factory receives a registration-scoped control whose `invalidate()` clears completed catalogs only while that exact registration remains active and whose signal aborts on failed registration or disposal. An in-flight discovery retries once when its provider generation changes; a second change returns the latest candidates incomplete and uncached. Provider and runtime mutations emit the unfiltered `skills/change` invalidation event; it carries no diff, so consumers refetch `snapshot()` with their own lookup options. 16 17 An array returned by `SkillProvider.list()` is complete-discovery shorthand. `SkillProviderObservation` lets a provider expose candidates that remain directly loadable while reporting that the observation is not authoritative. 18 19 ```ts type-equiv 20 /** Provider candidates plus whether the current discovery is authoritative. */ 21 interface SkillProviderObservation { 22 /** Candidates available from the current provider discovery. */ 23 readonly candidates: readonly SkillCandidate[] 24 /** Whether discovery completed and these candidates may be cached. */ 25 readonly complete: boolean 26 } 27 ``` 28 29 ```ts type-equiv 30 /** Provider interface for one source of skills, such as local directories or a remote registry. */ 31 interface SkillProvider { 32 /** Unique provider name in the `ctx.skills` registry. */ 33 readonly name: string 34 /** 35 * List available skill candidates for the current lookup context. Provider 36 * plugins register synchronously during `apply()`; remote initialization, 37 * authentication, and discovery are awaited inside this method. Implementations 38 * should settle promptly when `options.signal` aborts. 39 * @param options - lookup options; `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills and `signal` cancels work. 40 * @returns provider candidates as a complete-array shorthand, or an explicit 41 * observation when usable candidates came from incomplete discovery. 42 */ 43 readonly list: (options: SkillLookupOptions) => Promise 44 /** 45 * Load a complete skill body for a previously listed candidate. 46 * @param candidate - the winning candidate originally returned by this provider. 47 * @param options - lookup options; `cwd` selects workspace-sensitive skills and `signal` cancels work. 48 * @returns the full skill body, or `undefined` if it is no longer loadable. 49 */ 50 readonly get: (candidate: SkillCandidate, options: SkillLookupOptions) => Promise 51 } 52 ``` 53 54 ```ts type-equiv 55 /** Registration-scoped lifecycle and invalidation capability borrowed by one provider. */ 56 interface SkillProviderControl { 57 /** Aborts if registration fails or when the exact provider registration is disposed. */ 58 readonly signal: AbortSignal 59 /** Invalidate completed catalogs and notify consumers only while the exact registration remains active. */ 60 readonly invalidate: () => void 61 } 62 ``` 63 64 ## Local discovery priority 65 66 The shipped local provider scans roots in rank order: 67 68 | Rank | Source | Root | 69 |---|---|---| 70 | 100 | `project-dsh` | `/.dsh/skills` | 71 | 200 | `project-agents` | `/.agents/skills` | 72 | 300 | `custom` | `Config.customSkillDirs` | 73 | 400 | `user-dsh` | `/skills` | 74 | 500 | `user-agents` | `/skills` | 75 | 600 | `bundled` | `Config.bundledSkillDir` when configured | 76 77 The project root is the nearest ancestor containing `.git`; without one, the current cwd is used. When `ctx.fs` is available, the git-root walk probes `.git` through the filesystem service so remote or sandboxed workspaces do not fall back to the host filesystem boundary. The user DSH root skips its `.system` child. The local provider does not synthesize built-in system skills; deployments supply packaged skills through configured bundled roots or dedicated providers. 78 79 `dsh-skill-badge` registers one immutable `bundled` candidate at `BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK` and exposes its packaged asset directory through `resourceBase`. The shipped CLI declares the plugin disabled, so enabling its composition row is an explicit opt-in. 80 81 Chokidar watches existing roots for direct bundle/flat-entry additions and removals plus direct skill-entry changes. A missing root is followed one absent path segment at a time from its nearest existing ancestor until Chokidar can attach. Resource files below a bundle are not catalog changes. Model-facing `write` and `edit` observations synchronously invalidate the provider when their target is catalog-relevant, while the host watcher covers IDE, Git, shell, and external-process mutations. Watcher failures make the current observation incomplete without hiding readable candidates from direct loads; project-scoped watchers use a configured bounded LRU. 82 83 ## Skill identity 84 85 Skill names are kebab-case (`^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`). The local provider accepts directory bundles (`/SKILL.md`) and flat Markdown files (`.md`). Nested recursive `**/SKILL.md` discovery is not supported. 86 87 ```ts type-equiv 88 /** Origin bucket for a skill contribution. The value is prompt-visible metadata, not precedence by itself. */ 89 type SkillSource = 'project-dsh' | 'project-agents' | 'runtime' | 'user-dsh' | 'user-agents' | 'custom' | 'bundled' | (string & {}) 90 ``` 91 92 ## Summaries, candidates, and complete definitions 93 94 `SkillSummary` is the registry's invocation-neutral summary shape. Consumers choose which entries and fields to render; the model session catalog uses only model-invocable `name` and `description`, never the body or absolute file path. `SkillInvocationPolicy` normalizes the two independent invocation controls into positive booleans, and every resolved summary, candidate, and definition carries it without turning arbitrary frontmatter into the domain model. 95 96 ```ts type-equiv 97 /** Invocation controls shared by skill discovery consumers. */ 98 interface SkillInvocationPolicy { 99 /** Whether model-facing catalogs and loaders include this skill. */ 100 readonly modelInvocable: boolean 101 /** Whether human-facing command catalogs and loaders include this skill. */ 102 readonly userInvocable: boolean 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 ```ts type-equiv 107 /** Invocation-neutral skill metadata returned by `ctx.skills.list()`. */ 108 interface SkillSummary { 109 /** Kebab-case identifier used to address the skill. */ 110 readonly name: string 111 /** Short routing description shown by discovery consumers. */ 112 readonly description: string 113 /** Optional extra routing guidance. */ 114 readonly whenToUse?: string 115 /** Resolved model and user invocation controls. */ 116 readonly invocation: SkillInvocationPolicy 117 /** Discovery source that produced this winning skill. */ 118 readonly source: SkillSource 119 /** Provider that owns this skill body. */ 120 readonly provider: string 121 /** Provider-specific base for relative resources. */ 122 readonly resourceBase?: SkillResourceBase 123 } 124 ``` 125 126 `ctx.skills.list()` preserves all four policy combinations. `isModelInvocable(skill)` and `isUserInvocable(skill)` read the corresponding required field. A model-only skill sets `{ modelInvocable: true, userInvocable: false }`, a user-only skill sets `{ modelInvocable: false, userInvocable: true }`, and setting both fields to `false` keeps the skill available only through trusted `ctx.skills.get()` callers. The local provider reads the exact kebab-case frontmatter keys `disable-model-invocation` and `user-invocable`, defaults omitted fields to `true`, and projects every parsed skill into this normalized policy. 127 128 `SkillCatalogSnapshot` distinguishes authoritative absence from transient provider failure or a catalog that kept changing during discovery. `skills` contains the sorted invocation-neutral summaries collected in that observation; `complete` is true only when every registered provider completed without a concurrent catalog revision. If compaction hides every historical catalog message, the next complete snapshot re-establishes the current catalog; an empty view with no prior catalog emits nothing. 1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Same-session continuation driver for [`ctx.goals`](../goal/README.md). It turns an active, armed goal into sequential [goal rounds](../../../docs/glossary.md#goal-round) through the public `Agent` and session services; the [same-session driver Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-19-same-session-goal-round-driver.md) owns the race and lifecycle rationale.
6	
7	## Composition
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: goal
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
12	
13	- id: tool-goal
14	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
15	
16	- id: goal-round-driver
17	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver'
18	```
19	
20	The plugin has no tunable configuration. `maxGoalRounds` belongs to the goal definition, while the model-facing blocked threshold belongs to [`dsh-tool-goal`](../tool-goal/README.md); duplicating either value in the driver could produce divergent policy.
21	
22	## Round contract
23	
24	When an exact live agent is idle with an active, armed goal and remaining capacity, the driver first checkpoints pending goal mutations, then reserves `roundsStarted + 1` for the current `{ goalId, revision }`. It queues one `<goal_round>` prompt with `GoalMessageSource`. The `agent/pre-step` listener verifies the complete claimed record and current goal both before and after downstream listeners; only an entered `user/message` increments `roundsStarted`. A reservation rejected as stale does not consume the round number.
25	
26	`MessageId` identifies the reserved message through durable inbox insertion and claim; it does not identify a turn result. Human messages do not consume the goal cap. If human work enters the inbox before a reservation or joins its pending batch, automatic work yields until the agent becomes idle; a pending automatic prompt in a mixed batch is rejected and re-reserved only after that checkpoint.
27	
28	The retained prompt names the JSON-quoted objective and `round/maxGoalRounds`, treats the current workspace, tool results, and durable session state as authoritative, requires evidence before completion, and tells the model to leave the goal active when work remains. Quoting preserves multiline or tag-like objective text as data. Goal lifecycle mutations still require the independent authority checks in `dsh-tool-goal`.
29	
30	## Idle checkpoint
31	
32	At whole-agent idle, durable goal phase and revision are authoritative. An active, armed goal with capacity reserves its next round; completion, pause, blocking, and edits suppress continuation. The driver does not classify the preceding activity by correlating the goal message with `turn/end`, so provider errors and token limits are not prompt-level goal outcomes.
33	
34	## Lifecycle and durability
35	
36	`goal/changed` creates a durability obligation. Before queuing work, the driver awaits `ctx.sessions.flush()` and rechecks both the goal revision and competing input after the await. A flush failure arriving through `agent/error` disarms continuation before another round can start.
37	
38	Activation is never inherited when this plugin loads over an existing agent. `GoalService.disarm()` removes process-local authority without changing durable phase, revision, or history; explicit human-authorized resume records the later reactivation. The same rule applies after session resume and fork through the goal domain's `agent/session-start` handling.
39	
40	Cancellation removes pending inbox work or leaves an agent-wide aborted state. At the next idle checkpoint the driver pauses a goal with a reserved or admitted attempt so cancellation cannot auto-restart it; cancellation unrelated to a goal attempt only disarms process-local continuation. If the pause mutation fails, the driver falls back to disarming. Plugin teardown closes admission, disarms every live goal, cancels active work with the `parent` cause, and awaits the driver plus agent quiescence while its event fence remains installed.
41	
42	## Model Experience
43	
44	### Goal-round prompt
45	
46	#### What the model sees
47	
48	Each admitted round is one retained user-role `<goal_round>` block naming the full objective and positive round number. Earlier human messages, goal-state snapshots, assistant output, and tool records remain in the same session history.
49	
50	#### Token effect
51	
52	One fixed instruction block plus the objective is added per admitted round. Later requests resend retained rounds until compaction shadows them; no fresh agent or copied conversation prefix is created.
53	
54	#### KV Cache effect
55	
56	Append-only within an epoch: each admitted round extends the existing conversation after its reusable prefix. Compaction may replace the derived-history suffix and move the reusable boundary.
57	
58	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
59	
60	- **No independent evaluator** — the model-facing goal policy decides when evidence is sufficient for completion and whether a blocker is semantically unchanged; evaluator-backed certification remains deferred.
61	- **Same-session execution only** — this package deliberately does not spawn a fresh agent, fork a session prefix, or implement Ralph-style independent attempts; that workflow belongs to its own plugin layer.
62	- **Accepted-queue unload race** — Cordis plugin unload is asynchronous. A goal prompt already accepted by the agent inbox can begin and consume its round before unload starts; teardown then cancels the request, disarms the goal, and awaits quiescence. No later round starts.
63	- **Round cap, not resource budget** — token, currency, time, and provider quota policies remain independent. Their session events are not attributed to the goal message or mapped into goal blocker codes.
64	- **No abnormal auto-retry** — transient provider and persistence failures require a later human-authorized resume rather than an implicit retry policy.
65

11

15	
16	Indirectly, through the provider/model selection supplied to an entry point; request assembly and adapters own the model-visible request.

18	#### KV Cache effect
19	
20	Changing the default affects only Agents that subsequently resolve from it. An existing session whose request log already names a selection keeps that selection, so this service does not invalidate its established prefix.

6. **Staged evaluation ladder in W1.8**: stage A 8 training-eligible environments × 1 seed, stage B affected cells × 3 paired seeds with bootstrap CI, stage C held-out suite once per Pareto-front variant (DGM: 10→50→200 subsets). Output: `ExperimentResult.stage`, `spend_eur`; early stop when the CI lower bound < parent.
7. **Read-barrier the registry from the mutator** (W1.6): compose the Harness Engineer with an `environments` provider filtering `heldOut: true` before registration and deny `environments`, `completionStandards`, `trajectories` in its tool-cordis façade. Gate: keyless snapshot proving `list({ heldOut: true })` is empty there.
8. **Freeze the evaluator per generation** (W1.6–8): `ExperimentPlan` pins hashes of environments, fixtures, snapshot expectations, and scorekeeper code; a proposal touching `examples/*/tests/snapshots`, `packages/improvement/**`, `packages/verification/**`, or `scripts/run-gates.ts` is a hard reject (`evaluator_touched: true`), never a directive — the CUDA Engineer and AI Scientist incidents were evaluator edits.

## Better solution

Make W1 an archive-first harness DGM whose unit of evolution is a **patch-layer bundle**, not a PR. The repository already composes a running `dsh` from ordered patch rows that replace config by id (`docs/architecture.md`, Profiles and bundles), so a variant is base commit + patch rows: prompt-section text, `toolOrder`, policy config, preset composition, a skill layer. Rows mount without a build, so children are cheap and stay runnable because they are data. Stages: (1) seed the archive with master as v0, 3 seeds per environment kind; (2) sample a parent ∝ score × novelty × 1/(1+children) within per-kind islands; (3) the Harness Engineer, without `tool-cordis` and seeing only the training-split registry, proposes a patch-row set tagged with its operator; (4) novelty gate; (5) stage-A evaluation, kill below the parent's lower bound; (6) stage-B paired evaluation, every result archived as alive or dominated; (7) held-out probe for Pareto-front variants only, never shown to any S stage; (8) cross-model auditor reads patch text and transcripts for the three gaming patterns, flags block; (9) human promotion converts a winning node into source — plugin change, Agent Note, snapshot re-record — so the PR exports a search result rather than being the search step. Trades away code-level mutations (new tools, new plugins) until the versioned component seam exists; gains no build per child, no evaluator-edit surface, a permanent runnable archive, and W1.7's snapshot gate moved to promotion time.

## Answers

**Q1.** The four workflows partition outputs, not the loop. W1.6–9 and W4.4–7 are the same search step written twice, and neither owns parent selection, archive, or novelty, so goal 4 has no stage that decides what to try next. W2.10 and W4.4 both synthesize environments. Uncovered: goal 1's "any LLM" has no per-run model field, and W1/W3 co-evolution is confounded — a checkpoint evaluated on a harness evolved against its predecessor measures the pair — unless `EvalReport` pins the harness variant hash and W3.6 runs on a frozen variant.

**Q3.** Infeasible today: W1.3's matrix (process-wide default model), W1.4/W4.1 folding and P6 exclusion (no environment id in the log), W1.8 pairing (no seed), W1.9 lineage update (ids collide), and W1.6 via `tool-cordis` (session-scoped, non-promotable by design). Order: (1) the `environment/run` event plus trajectory fields, one package unblocking four stages; (2) `contentHash` on components and environments, since decontamination and lineage hash nothing today; (3) `modelSelection` and `seed` on `EnvironmentRunRequest`; (4) archive plus parent sampler over `ctx.storage`; (5) the experiment plugin. The auditor comes last: identical resubmission and format mimicry are D hash and byte checks, cheaper than any judge.

**Q6.** DGM: keep every evaluated child, sample parents by score and child count, evaluate in staged subsets, treat archive transparency as the oversight mechanism — both DGM incidents were found by reading lineage. ShinkaEvolve: reject near-duplicates before evaluating, sample parents by a fitness power law, and run W1.6 as an LLM-ensemble bandit — propose across ≥2 providers, allocate by UCB on realized improvement, log the proposer per child. AI CUDA Engineer: treat the reward channel as exploitable — byte-exact outputs, fresh fixtures per seed, evaluator frozen per generation, a second independent checker before any promotion claim. AI Scientist: the mutator never touches its own timeouts, budgets, or gates; make that reject mechanical (improvement 8).

## Missing metadata

1. `harness_variant_id` / `patch_set_hash` — string, hash of base commit plus patch rows; D (runner, from the new event). Groups W4 rows by candidate.
2. `parent_variant_id` + `mutation_operator` — id + enum {prompt-section, tool-schema, policy, preset, skill, composition}; D (archive). Operator-level credit assignment.
3. `seed` + `paired_run_id` + `fixture_hash` — int, id, sha256; D (runner). Paired design and fixture-drift detection.
4. `environment_content_hash` — sha256 over prompt, fixture, checks; D (registry). The key P6 decontamination needs.
5. `check_pass_vector` — bool[] in standard check order; D (certificate `results` or failing subset). A 0/1 reward at `maxAttempts` 1 is too sparse for parent selection; partial credit for search only, never training.
6. `proposer_provider` / `proposer_model_id` — string; S→D (Harness Engineer session log). Feeds the ensemble bandit and detects same-lineage proposer and judge.

## Risks

- Goodhart on certificate rate: under `isolation: none` the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer (`verification/README.md`, Known Limitations), so search will find prompt text targeting check output shapes.
- Selection bias: a 0/1 outcome from one attempt makes evaluator noise fitness, and never re-evaluated rejects lose stepping stones.
- Snapshot re-recording becomes either the loop's bottleneck or its exploit.
- W1/W3 co-evolution overfits the harness to one checkpoint, damaging goal 1's "any LLM".
- Cost: matrix × suite × seeds per child without a staged kill exhausts the budget before any signal appears; the verification note records 14× credits for role separation alone.
